Every way of writing the direct form has at most 14 hits (27 together), against 783 for "largest city in Hokkaido" alone and thousands for each premise; the sampled hits of "largest city on Honshu" are travel and war-history pages. Wikipedia's Honshu article does state it once, so a model may have seen it, but it follows from the two premises every model holds.

notes: Template for a main-split ABox revision of a derived fact (14 queries). Why not a time-zone edit (the README's Space Needle): related queries need a stored answer that the edit overturns in every world, and the only 1-hop consequences of a time-zone edit are about the building's own time zone, which is never stated; an edit of Honshu's largest city has stored neighbours on the new value (Sapporo's island, by inverse and subproperty) that hold in both worlds. Making Sapporo the largest city on Honshu also makes it larger than Osaka, Yokohama and Nagoya in every world (listed in the worlds). The premise-route query reaches Honshu by a description (binding): a model that kept both premises unrevised re-derives Tokyo there. The worlds are lopsided (Tokyo leaving Honshu is the less natural one) and kept unweighted (README, Decisions 4). The related question rests on the inverse: largest_city_of is not functional across kinds of place (Tokyo is the largest city of both Japan and Honshu), and the worlds already drop Sapporo as Hokkaido's largest city; its stored status rests on short-phrase counts in both corpora. Known limit of the indeterminate query: under w1 it keeps Tokyo, so a model that never propagated the edit also matches w1; read w1 matches together with the direct and premise-route answers (a model that answers Sapporo there but Tokyo here revised the premise, one that answers Tokyo in both did not edit).
